findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "my_schedule" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Classes for a week at the signed-in member's gyms (all of them, or one with gym), with the class ids book_class needs (structured classId only: do not show it),…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_gyms, get_gym, get_schedule, get_prices, search_classes, get_my_account, my_gyms · Public sink: search_gyms, get_gym, get_schedule, get_prices, start_trial, search_classes, checkout_status, get_my_account, my_gyms, my_bookings, my_schedule, book_class, cancel_booking · Destructive: search_classes.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_gyms, get_gym, get_schedule, get_prices, search_classes, get_my_account, my_gyms · Public sink: search_gyms, get_gym, get_schedule, get_prices, start_trial, search_classes, checkout_status, get_my_account, my_gyms, my_bookings, my_schedule, book_class, cancel_booking · Destructive: search_classes

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
